answer: An identity's sonnet is sealed by a beacon chip cut for it alone, and the chip must carry a verifier for every sonnet its holder sealed before, the garden keeping one row per holder so a fresh wallet inherits the earlier chips. Verifiers add die area and fab yield collapses as area grows, so the newest seal costs more than all its earlier seals together. A newcomer buys one small chip; an operator holding a thousand identities must buy wafer for half a million bespoke dies.
